P2.2

There are 2026 playing cards arranged in a row, each card having a front face and a back face. Initially, all cards are face up. Alice and Bob take turns performing the following operation, with Alice going first: the current player selects 50 adjacent cards such that the leftmost card is face up, and flips all 50 cards. The player who cannot make a move loses. Who has a winning strategy?

Solution: Bob has a winning strategy, and the strategy is to flip arbitrarily. Let face up be and face down be .

First, if we view the cards from left to right as a binary number, the number strictly decreases after each operation, so the game is guaranteed to terminate.

Now, view all cards from right to left as a sequence , and consider . Initially, . Each time 50 adjacent cards are flipped, exactly one is flipped, changing the parity of . Thus, whenever it is Bob's turn, is always odd, meaning there exists some , so Bob is guaranteed to have a valid move. Q.E.D.!
